outcome.technical: Added _harness.gone_within(target, seconds, group=False) (polls, >=1 look; pid judged by _locks.pid_alive plus a zombie reading via /proc/<pid>/stat state Z or `ps -o stat=`; group judged by killpg(0) plus `ps -A -o pgid=,stat=` members not Z). VERIFIED: _locks.pid_alive (scripts/governance/_locks.py:150) is os.kill(pid,0) so it counts a zombie ALIVE; the zombie reading is test-side knowledge, product rule untouched (case asserts product pid_alive is True for the unreaped zombie). is4 now uses gone_within(grandchild,10); test__proc_group drops _group_gone_within and uses gone_within(...,group=True). New case lv0 in test_run_test_gate.py, titled with the tests.add clause verbatim plus detail after ' (': fixtures = unreaped child exiting 0.6s later (first look sees running, helper returns True), group fixture, own pid not gone; AST scan _single_look_reads over every tests/*.py flags os.kill/os.killpg(x,0) in a scope (function or module body, nested functions excluded) that calls a kill-shaped name on an earlier line; reads in scopes with no earlier kill are allowed, as are _harness._pid_present/_group_present; synthetic bad/fine/home sources pin both directions. Mutations in scratch copy (restore asserted: real tree green 540/540 and deadline line present): helper looks once -> case red; is4 reverted to sleep+single os.kill -> case red with offenders={'test_run_test_gate.py': [...]}. Runs: test__proc_group x5 exit 0 each; test_run_test_gate 540/540 exit 0; test__refs 351/351 after replacing a literal /proc path (ar1 caught it); full sweep exit 0 (335/335 files); cp1252 sweep exit 0.
